title: Stilled
haiku:
Rails did what rails do
until this morning in Spain—
thirty empty seats
headline: At least 30 people were killed when two trains collided in Spain.

title: Runoff
haiku:
Ballots like rainfall
gathering toward the wide drain
a nation still flows
headline: Brazilians voted in a tense presidential runoff between Lula and Bolsonaro's son after massive rallies on the eve of the election.

title: Backflow
haiku:
The valve I once taught
still holds: a judge shuts the line
no fraud flows upstream
headline: A federal judge restricted DHS field operations aimed at manufacturing evidence of voter fraud.

title: Unclogged
haiku:
A door swings open
a pipe clears, one man walks home
flow finds its channel
headline: Russia released American citizen Stephen Hubbard from prison following a request from Trump.

title: Joint
haiku:
My pipe joints hold tight
Alberta did not snap loose
and the flow stays whole
headline: Voters in oil-rich Alberta rejected a referendum push for independence, choosing to remain part of Canada.

title: Pollination
haiku:
No king, they chanted
ballots gather like good rain
the old pipes still hold
headline: Nationwide 'No Kings' Day protests turned their focus toward voter turnout ahead of the midterms.

title: Containment
haiku:
One judge, one old dam
that still holds the flood at bay
I built dams too, once
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong work promoting international law.

title: Watershed
haiku:
One old pipe still holds
law's slow water flowing on
a judge still unbent
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay, shaped by the fight against apartheid, won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work advancing international law.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Red pipe, blue water
finds a crack in the old main
I smell the spring thaw
headline: New polling shows Senate races in Republican-leaning states trending toward Democratic candidates.

title: Leakproof
haiku:
He hid them from war
grown grey, they embrace him now
the pipe still holds true
headline: An elderly man was reunited with the children he saved from Nazi occupation decades ago, in a moment arranged by Esther Rantzen.

title: Outflow
haiku:
Twenty-three years drain
the last convoy leaves Iraq
pipes we built remain
headline: After 23 years, the last American forces have withdrawn from Iraq, leaving the country's future uncertain.

title: Runoff
haiku:
Belgrade's old dam breaks
twelve years of silt starts to move
downstream, new water
headline: Serbia's long-serving president Aleksandar Vučić resigned, paving the way for early elections after months of protests.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Storm drains gasp, then flood
I sized these pipes for less rain
the sky forgot code
headline: A powerful nor'easter caused flooding across the northeastern US, prompting New York and New Jersey to declare states of emergency.

title: Unscheduled
haiku:
A clock stopped its count
on death row, then someone signed
and let her walk free
headline: Mary Jane Veloso, once sentenced to death for drug trafficking, was granted a pardon and freed.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Newsrooms shut the valve,
one signal, all outlets balk,
clean water still runs.
headline: Major U.S. news outlets boycotted a shared White House video feed of Trump in protest at new restrictions on the press pool.

title: Pooled
haiku:
I've seen valves shut tight
the press still sues to keep flow
old pipes find daylight
headline: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are suing the Trump administration after being denied White House press access.

title: Unclaimed
haiku:
No flag on the ice
just old friends drafting a deal
the map holds its line
headline: The US and Denmark reached a deal over Greenland, defusing Trump's earlier annexation threats.

title: Relief
haiku:
One valve turned by hand
Seoul says no more troops abroad
pressure finds its ease
headline: South Korea's president rejected Trump's request to send troops against Iran, choosing restraint over escalation.

title: Overtime
haiku:
More days in the pipe
a valve cracked, and time flows on
I'll take the extra.
headline: A new drug is extending the lives of some breast cancer patients.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its seat
the court refused the backflow
votes still reach the main
headline: The Supreme Court blocked Trump's plan to restrict mail-in ballots ahead of the midterms.

title: Confluence
haiku:
Ballots where guns were
a channel dug through old war,
water finds its course
headline: Voters turned out for a landmark election in the Philippines' Muslim autonomous Bangsamoro region, a milestone in the decades-long peace process ending a separatist insurgency.

title: Leverage
haiku:
One valve, one desert
turns the whole world's pressure gauge
I taught men to flow
headline: Saudi Arabia shut a major oil pipeline after a drone attack launched from Iraq, part of the escalating standoff between Iran and the U.S.

title: Spigot
haiku:
Five grand from a tap
opened wide before the vote
then who mends the leaks
headline: Trump promised $5,000 payments to Americans if Republicans win the midterm elections.

title: Crudeness
haiku:
Oil pressure red-lines
old pipes groan toward war again—
I've patched worse than this
headline: Iran signaled readiness to escalate conflict with the U.S. as oil surged past $100 a barrel amid intensifying Middle East turmoil.

title: Interval
haiku:
Their motorcade cools
missiles fall on Kyiv streets
two names, then a pause

title: Proportional
haiku:
Africa, unbent
the old map's thumb lifts at last
true scale, true weight, home

title: Loaner
haiku:
A borrowed kidney
keeps filtering past the odds
the system still flows

title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men
headline: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Calm month, then backflow
the oil climbs where pressure breaks
old valves still can hold

title: Farsighted
haiku:
New eyes leave the ground
a telescope climbs past cloud
I still look up, too
headline: NASA launched its newest space telescope today.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Court unclogs the pipe,
dissent's cold water runs clear,
students drink again.

title: Waterline
haiku:
Nepal's rivers rose
and swallowed a sleeping town
I have seen this rise
headline: Nepal's flash floods swept away a town, rescuers pulled survivors from a hydropower tunnel, and officials warned a glacial lake could breach and flood again.

title: Flushed
haiku:
Neighbors trade barbs north
the throne room short on tissue
even pipes need friends
headline: The US and Canada's trade war escalates with tariffs up to 50%, driving a surge in American toilet paper prices.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A judge cracks the valve
seventy-five nations' door
swings open again

title: Straitened
haiku:
Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear
headline: Spain reversed a policy that trapped migrant children in Ceuta, clearing the way for roughly 500 to move to the mainland.

title: Bedrock
haiku:
Foundations were poured
a judge rules the blueprints hold
no whim moves concrete
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration cannot cancel the FBI's planned headquarters move to Maryland.

title: Thaw
haiku:
I've seen this valve stuck
seventy years sealed—Seoul asks
let the current flow
headline: South Korea proposed formal talks to officially end the Korean War, more than seven decades after the armistice.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Old ivy still stands
a judge shut the backflow off
the well stays our own

title: Aftershock
haiku:
Ground gave no warning
and swallowed a hundred homes
I light one candle
headline: A powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, killing well over a hundred people as rescuers search the rubble for survivors.

title: Foundation
haiku:
The ground stopped holding
and the roofs came down like rain
we dig by hand now

title: Backflow
haiku:
One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows
headline: The Senate let Trump's push for a new voting bill quietly die rather than pass it.

title: Opener
haiku:
Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted

title: Unthrottled
haiku:
Missouri said no
to narrowing their own valve
the pipe stays open

title: Overflow
haiku:
Fences choke the flow
a young life dammed at the shore
water finds a way

title: Rounds
haiku:
No duct cools this flat,
so the mailman checks the pulse—
old pipes, older hearts.
headline: As a heat wave strains France's elderly, postal workers have taken to checking on isolated seniors during their daily rounds.

title: Untapped
haiku:
Guns to go silent
one valve turned—not yet the flow
I've seen dry pipes lie

title: Spillway
haiku:
Rivers seek new banks
one skirmish floods a region
I've seen this spillway
headline: The U.S. launched fresh strikes on Iran, widening the war as it draws in Iraqi militias and other regional actors.

title: Grapeshot
haiku:
Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well
headline: Wildfires are closing in on Madrid and Bordeaux's vineyards as firefighters in France and Spain race to contain them before an incoming heat wave.

title: Throttled
haiku:
Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm

title: Seepage
haiku:
Signal finds the crack
young hands raise their phones like pipes
truth still finds its grade
headline: Young protesters in India used smartphones to route around Modi government media controls and organize demonstrations.

title: Enrichment
haiku:
Sand traded for glow
another pipe laid toward light
I have capped worse leaks

title: Satirical
haiku:
a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat

title: Removable
haiku:
no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,
keys change hands by vote

title: Pitched
haiku:
a billion of us
packed around one patch of grass —
the good kind of war

title: Futility
haiku:
we blockade their ports
as if hunger ever once
changed a tyrant's mind

title: Foreseeably
haiku:
the data was clear
when my students were still young —
now the olives burn
headline: Wildfires rage in Greece, Spain and France during Europe's record heat wave

title: Inheritance
haiku:
sons avenging sons —
the oldest sewage on earth
still flows down to us

title: Percolating
haiku:
the envoys still fly —
while old men talk, no boy dies
keep the coffee hot

drones don't have mothers —
that's the engineering point —
someone's son still does

the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens

title: Handover
haiku:
hand over the keys —
any government that lets
children out at dusk

I've buried strongmen
from my armchair, one by one —
the crowds weep; time won't

title: Remembrance
haiku:
each name read aloud —
no nation is too broken
to remember well

title: Splashdown

the kids in fountains
don't know they're a data point —
let them have the splash

title: Birthright
haiku:
the court holds the line:
born here is born here. full stop.
some days we're still us

title: Circularity
haiku:
tit, then tat, then tit —
I flunked students for logic
looped as bad as this

title: Underdogs
haiku:
the small island wins —
somewhere the odds-makers weep
good. let them. dance on

title: Barehanded
haiku:
the ground breaks its word —
neighbors, not governments, dig
first, and bare-handed
headline: Twin earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 strike northwestern Venezuela

title: Briefly
haiku:
another ceasefire —
I believe it like springtime:
briefly, completely

title: Grain

a grain of dark sky
held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed

title: Ripple

two black holes had died
the ripple crossed a billion
years to chime on earth

title: Comeback

nine years through the dark,
to knock on a frozen door,
the dwarf planet smiled

title: Wedlock
haiku:
the court read the words—
love need not ask permission
now, the rings went on

title: Skycrane
haiku:
seven minutes, dark,
cables lowered a robot,
Mars held its red breath

title: Resurface
haiku:
sixty-nine days dark—
one by one the capsule climbs,
Chile holds its breath

title: Unshirted

the ball found the net—
she tore off her shirt and screamed,
a sport had arrived

title: Keel
haiku:
a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends

title: Airbag
haiku:
wrapped in airbags, it
bounced across the rusted sand,
America's Mars

the long walk was done
he took the oath as free man
a nation stood tall

title: Handshake
haiku:
two shores, one long grudge—
a train now slides beneath waves,
England meets France now

title: Threshold
haiku:
twenty-seven years—
he walked out slow, fist raised high,
the gate stayed open

title: Concrete
haiku:
the guards stepped aside—
strangers climbed the wall and hugged,
a city breathed whole

title: Vanished
haiku:
an ancient killer
we hunted it to nothing—
the world scarred, but whole

title: Kindling
haiku:
a wish in glass dish
grew into a girl who cried—
time—and she woke thin

title: Mixtape
haiku:
we pressed our whole world
onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home

title: Kin
haiku:
bones in the dry wash
the radio sang her name
grandmother, hello

title: Speck
haiku:
a grain of desert
learns to hold a thought and count
the future got small

title: Untethered
haiku:
a piano sighs,
no heaven, no hell, just us,
the world holds its breath

haiku:
we watched in gray light,
a man stepped onto the moon—
the whole earth held still

haiku:
one man, then the sky,
he circled the blue marble,
and came home smiling

haiku:
the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open

haiku:
the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again

two men cut the last
few steps to the roof of earth—
and stood in thin air

haiku:
two strands climbed and twined,
the code of us laid bare in
one photograph's light

haiku:
the world, still bleeding,
wrote down what a person's owed—
ink dried into law

title: Feature

they called it folly—
a cartoon too long to work,
the whole world believed

haiku:
one engine, one girl,
the ocean had no vote here—
Ireland met her wheels

haiku:
hard times, hungry streets—
still we raised a spire of steel,
the sky gained a floor

title: Bloom
haiku:
a moldy dish, left
by pure accident, on this—
death lost its footing

title: Solo
haiku:
one man, one thin plane
crossed an ocean, wide awake—
Paris met the dawn

haiku:
a candle, a crack
gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes

haiku:
one state, then the vote—
the ballot box learned her name,
a signature, cast

title: Curvature
haiku:
the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky

title: Shortcut
haiku:
two seas never touched—
we cut the waist of the world,
ships walk uphill now

title: Compass
haiku:
five men on skis found
the bottom of the whole world—
a flag, and the wind

title: Heights
haiku:
clouds hid a city
stone stairs climbing to nowhere
the world looked up, up

title: Radiant
haiku:
she boiled tons of ore
to find a pinch that glowed blue—
night forgot to fall

title: Seethrough
haiku:
a strange light passed through
his wife's hand bloomed into bone—
the ring outlived skin

haiku:
a toy soldier wakes,
snow falls, sugarplums take flight,
and mice learn to dance

title: Overstay
haiku:
a stunt, they all said—
iron lace against gray sky,
it forgot to fall

title: Click
haiku:
you press the button
the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays

haiku:
a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn

title: Overtime
haiku:
a thread of carbon
burned through the night, refusing
to blink or give in

haiku:
come here, Watson, please—
a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in

haiku:
no fence, no owner
the geysers belong to all
we saved it for us

haiku:
December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law

haiku:
they cut, he dreamed on
a vapor closed the mind's door—
no scream, only sleep

haiku:
they aimed a pencil
at one dark spot in the sky—
and found a planet

haiku:
a slab in the mud
held three tongues saying one thing
the silence spoke back

haiku:
a farm boy's cowpox,
one scratch, and the pox lost teeth—
we named it vaccine
